chunks: Abu Ahmad al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Siraj in Hamedan narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Tabi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdul Aziz al-Dinawari narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Abasi narrated from Sufyan al-Thawri, saying: I met the Truthful, son of the Truthful, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them).

So I said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, advise me. He said to me: O Sufyan, there is no chivalry for a liar, no brotherhood for kings, and no rest for the envious, nor mastery for the ill-natured. I said: O son of the Messenger of God, add to me. He said to me: O Sufyan, trust in God and you will be a believer, and be content with what God has decreed for you and you will be rich, and treat your neighbor well and you will be a Muslim, and do not associate with the wicked so that he teaches you his wickedness, and consult in your affairs those who fear God, the Mighty and Exalted.

So I said: O son of the Messenger of God, add to me. He said to me: O Sufyan, whoever desires honor without a tribe, wealth without property, and majesty without authority, let him transfer himself from the humiliation of God's disobedience to the honor of His obedience.

So I said: Add to me, O son of the Messenger of God. He said to me: O Sufyan, my father (peace be upon him) commanded me to do three things and forbade me from three things. Among what he said to me was: O my son, whoever associates with the companion of evil will not be safe, and whoever enters the places of evil will be suspected, and whoever does not control his tongue will regret.

Then he recited to me [saying] (peace be upon him): Accustom your tongue to saying good, and you will gain it. For the tongue accustoms itself to whatever you accustom it to. You are liable for what you have trained it to do, in good and evil, so see how you accustom it.
ai.seo_question: What ethical advice did Imam al-Sadiq give to Sufyan al-Thawri regarding character and social conduct?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Khisal* highlights the transmission of ethical wisdom from Imam al-Sadiq to the prominent jurist Sufyan al-Thawri, illustrating the cross-school respect for Ahl al-Bayt's moral authority. The Imam’s advice synthesizes spiritual contentment (*rida*) with social prudence, warning that associating with the wicked corrupts one’s character and that uncontrolled speech leads to regret, a theme deeply rooted in Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* as the foundation of faith.
